podcast.title: Portland Supergroup Attempt (circa 1985)
podcast.body: Sugar Baby Doll was formed in Portland around 1985, featuring a lineup of strong personalities: former stripper Courtney Love, screaming guitarist Cat Bjelland from Minneapolis, and LA bassist Jennifer Finch. The band's inability to "hold it together" due to these personalities led to its quick breakup in late 1985, with members moving on to form other notable bands. "Sugar Baby Doll was formed down the coast in Portland in about 1985."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: No Surviving Official Recordings
podcast.body: Despite word spreading about the kind of music Sugar Baby Doll was attempting to create, there appear to be no surviving official recordings of the band. However, some material from Pagan Babies, formed by Courtney Love and Cat Bjelland after Sugar Baby Doll's demise, might have been part of their live sets. "Like I said, there doesn't seem to be any surviving official Sugar Baby Doll recordings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Riot Grrrl Band
podcast.body: Sugar Baby Doll is mentioned as one of the bands within the Riot Grrrl movement. "And then there were bands like Sugar Baby Doll and the Pagan Babies and Brat Mobio and Heaven's De Betsy and Huggy Bear."

xref.title: Early Career as a Stripper
xref.body: Prior to her involvement in Sugar Baby Doll and later bands, Courtney Love was described as a former stripper. Her strong personality was noted as a factor in Sugar Baby Doll's inability to remain together as a band. "The lineup featured a former stripper named Courtney Love"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: LA Bass Player Joins L7
xref.body: Jennifer Finch, an LA bass player, was a member of Sugar Baby Doll. After that band's breakup, she ended up joining L7, an all-female grunge band. "and an LA bass player named Jennifer Finch."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Sugar Baby Doll Collaboration
xref.body: After Sugar Baby Doll broke up in late 1985, Courtney Love and Cat Bjelland stayed together to form a new group called Pagan Babies. This band was another "pre-Riot Grrrl band" and, despite its brief existence, represents a link in the early collaborations of these influential musicians. "But when the band broke up in late 1985, Courtney and Cat stayed together long enough to be in a new group called Pagan Babies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pre-Hole Career and Struggles
xref.body: Before finding her place with Hole, Courtney Love was involved in several bands, including Sugar Baby Doll and Babes in Toilet. She also had a very brief stint as the singer for Faith No More, lasting "about 15 minutes" before she was kicked out. To support herself and her early band efforts, she engaged in arts, acting, and stripping, using the money from stripping to purchase gear for her band. "She'd been in a bunch of bands with names like Sugar Baby Doll and Babes in Toilet."
